newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close lower on government's tax stand.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close lower on government's tax stand.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) closed lower after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram defended the proposed minimum alternate tax (MAT) on high-growth companies, brokers said.
The DSE sensitive index ended 9.07 points lower at 766.99.
"Finance Minister's rejection to withdraw MAT was the major reason behind the fall in the share prices," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Monday defended the imposition of MAT, which would require high-growth companies to pay a minimum tax on their profits.
Several Indian blue chip firms often seek exemptions from payment of taxes by showing fresh capital expenditure.
Financial markets still expect Chidambaram to announce some exemptions to the MAT, included in the proposed 1996/97 Finance Bill.
Chidambaram is scheduled to begin his reply on the Finance Bill on Tuesday.
Reliance Industries dropped 0.60 rupee to 207.40, while TISCO ended 2.50 rupees lower at 187.35 rupees following selling by foreign institutional investors, brokers said.
State Bank of India fell 0.40 rupee to 276.90 and Oriental Bank of Commerce quoted 0.65 rupee down at 82.90.
ACC was down 65 rupees to 2,055 while TELCO lost 14 rupees to 475 on selling by mutual funds, brokers said.
ITC eased 0.95 rupee to 296.20 and Hindustan Lever slipped 9.95 rupees to 810.25.
Larsen and Toubro quoted 0.40 rupee lower at 248.45.
